## GET /admin-api/saml-idp-initiated

`getSamlIdpInitiatedApplications`

**The SAML applications a sign-in may be started here for, with each one's link**

Every SAML 2.0 service provider and SAML 1.1 relying party in this realm for which an identity-provider-initiated sign-in would be ALLOWED: the realm's `saml2.idpInitiatedSso` / `saml11.idpInitiatedSso` (off by default), unless the entry's `saml2IdpInitiatedSso` / `saml11IdpInitiatedSso` says otherwise — asked through the function `GET /launch/{app}` asks, so a row here is never one the link refuses with STS-LAUNCH-0005. One row per application and family; an application on in both is two rows.

`launchUrl` is the link a person follows (`/launch/{app}?protocol=`, this realm's, on the sign-in service's listener) and `endpoint` the protocol's own unsolicited endpoint the link hands the browser to. A row whose `missing` is not empty is switched on and cannot work yet — it has no registered assertion consumer service, and the link answers STS-LAUNCH-0006 — and is listed so that it can be fixed.

`realmSwitches` says whether each realm setting is on: with both off, only an entry's own override can put a row here.

Paged on `idpInitiatedPage` and `per`, by identifier.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/saml2` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `idpInitiatedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `idpInitiated` to return, answered by `idpInitiatedPaging`. The applications, by identifier. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |

**200**: One page of the applications, its paging and the realm's two switches.

## GET /admin-api/saml2

`getSaml2ServiceProviders`

**Every SAML 2.0 service provider, and the endpoints each is configured from**

A full SAML 2.0 identity provider: HTTP Redirect, HTTP POST and HTTP POST SimpleSign for the AuthnRequest, and HTTP POST, HTTP Redirect, HTTP POST SimpleSign or HTTP Artifact for the Response, with a SOAP artifact resolution service behind the last.

**Every service provider gets its own identity provider metadata** — a distinct entityID and its own endpoints — and **in development a document is minted for any entityID asked for**, so nothing has to be provisioned before a service provider can be pointed at this service; in product every per-service-provider path is a 404 for an entityID that is not registered. That is why `metadataUrl` is on every row rather than being one constant.

This resource holds nothing: every row is an entry in `ou=applications`, the same one `GET /admin-api/applications` reports.

`?sp=<entityID>` returns one of them, with what has been recorded about it — and answers 200 with `found: false` for an entityID that is not registered — whose metadata is still served and whose AuthnRequest would still be answered, in development only.

The list reply carries `mdqRefused`: the entityIDs a request asked the Metadata Query responder to register and product mode refused (no trust anchor, or an answer that did not verify), newest first, paged by `mdqRefusedPage`.

The `?sp=` reply also says what checking its requests' signatures found (`lastRequestVerification`), what they are verified against (`signingCertificates`), the certificate a request carried that nobody has confirmed (`observedSigningCertificate`), whether signed requests are required of it and why (`signedRequestsRequired`), and everything consuming its metadata registered (`metadata`).

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/saml2` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sp` | query | string |  | One service provider, by its entityID. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `mdqRefusedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `mdqRefused` to return, answered by `mdqRefusedPaging`. The Metadata Query lookups refused in product mode (#112), newest first. |

**200**: The service providers with the paging that found them, or one of them with its endpoints and its record.

## POST /admin-api/saml2/confirm-signing-certificate

`confirmSaml2SigningCertificate`

**Trust the certificate a signed request carried**

A signed request's `ds:KeyInfo` certificate that is not registered is recorded as OBSERVED (`observedSigningCertificate` on `GET /admin-api/saml2?sp=`, the attribute `samlObservedSigningCertificate`) and verifies NOTHING — anybody can sign a request and attach the key that verifies it. Development mode still encrypts an assertion to it when nothing else is on the entry; product does not.

This MOVES it onto `samlSigningCertificate`, so this service provider's signatures are verified against it from the next request. Refused when nothing is observed, and for a certificate whose key signs nothing this service verifies. Confirm only a key you know is the service provider's: this is the registration.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/saml2` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| `sp` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The application entry as it now stands.

## POST /admin-api/saml2/discard-signing-certificate

`discardSaml2SigningCertificate`

**Discard the certificate a signed request carried**

## POST /admin-api/saml2/mdq-import

`importSaml2MetadataFromMdq`

**Import a service provider from the MDQ responder**

Asks `saml2.mdqBaseUrl` for `<base>/entities/<percent-encoded entityID>` (the Metadata Query Protocol), and — when the answer describes that entity — creates the application entry if it does not exist and consumes the document, held to the realm's `saml2.metadataTrustAnchors`. Refused with no responder configured; an entry it created is removed again if the document is refused. **In product mode with no trust anchor it is refused** unless `saml2.mdqImportWithoutAnchors` is on, and then the reply carries `warnings`: the document was consumed with no signature check.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/saml2` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

## POST /admin-api/saml2/register

`registerSaml2ServiceProvider`

**Register a service provider by entityID**

OPTIONAL, and it changes nothing about whether a request is accepted: this identity provider accepts any entityID, and the first AuthnRequest or metadata fetch creates the entry anyway. What registering early buys is a metadata document to hand somebody before they have sent anything.

It is refused for an entityID that is already in the registry — an identifier names ONE application here whatever protocol brought it, so the answer to "it is already there" is to change what it holds rather than to create it twice.

## POST /admin-api/saml2/remove-signing-certificate

`removeSaml2SigningCertificate`

**Take one registered signing certificate off a service provider**

By value — the base64 DER exactly as `GET /admin-api/saml2?sp=` lists it in `signingCertificates` (a PEM is accepted and normalised). ## POST /admin-api/saml2/set-logout-service

`addSaml2LogoutService`

**Declare where this service provider's LogoutResponse goes**

A `<samlp:LogoutRequest>` CARRIES NO RETURN ADDRESS — only SP metadata does. The SingleLogoutService endpoints of the service provider's CONSUMED metadata are used first; with none, what is declared here; then the profile falls back to `saml2.defaultSingleLogoutService` and then to the assertion consumer service URL that service provider last used, WHICH IS A GUESS and is logged as one. It writes `samlSingleLogoutService` on the application entry, so an `ldapmodify` of the same attribute does exactly this — two doors onto one value, not two stores.

## POST /admin-api/saml2/set-metadata-signing-certificate

`setSaml2MetadataSigningCertificate`

Writes `samlSpMetadataSigningCertificate`. With it set, consuming a metadata document — a refresh or an upload — REFUSES one that is unsigned or whose signature does not verify against this certificate, and changes nothing. ## POST /admin-api/saml2/set-signing-certificate

`setSaml2SigningCertificate`

**Replace the certificates this service provider's signatures are verified against**

**THE TRUST ANCHOR FOR THIS SERVICE PROVIDER'S SIGNATURES** (2026-09-17). A signed AuthnRequest, LogoutRequest or LogoutResponse from it is VERIFIED against `samlSigningCertificate` in every mode, and refused when it verifies against none — never against the certificate the request carries. The attribute is a LIST (a metadata rollover publishes two keys); this REPLACES it with the one certificate given, and an empty `value` clears it. Consuming the service provider's metadata writes the same list.

Base64 DER or PEM — the armour and whitespace are stripped, because what the attribute holds is what a `ds:X509Certificate` carries. A value that is not a certificate whose key makes an XML signature this service verifies (RSA, EC, EdDSA, DSA, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) is refused and nothing changes: an unusable certificate would make every signature from this service provider fail. Public key material, worth nothing to whoever reads the directory.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/saml2` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/saml2/upload-metadata

`uploadSaml2Metadata`

**Consume a service provider's metadata document**

The same CONSUMPTION `POST /admin-api/applications/refresh-metadata` performs on a fetched document, for a document given here — a service provider whose metadata this service cannot reach. It REGISTERS what the `<md:SPSSODescriptor>` says: every AssertionConsumerService (binding, location, index, isDefault) as a return address — an AuthnRequest is then answered only at one of them, by index, by URL or by default, in every mode — every SingleLogoutService, every signing certificate (`use="signing"` or no `use`) as what its requests are verified against, the encryption certificate, its NameIDFormats (a NameIDPolicy naming another is then InvalidNameIDPolicy), and AuthnRequestsSigned and WantAssertionsSigned. The EFFECTIVE validUntil (earliest in the chain) is enforced — past it every request from the service provider is refused — and past the cacheDuration a document with a URL is fetched again in the background. An EntitiesDescriptor is read for this entity. The protocol URI is selected from the application declaration: SAML 1.1 is selected only for an entry declared for `saml11` and not `saml2`; SAML 2.0 remains the choice for SAML 2.0, dual-protocol and undeclared entries unless `family` explicitly selects one declared SAML family. This operation can therefore consume SAML 1.1-only metadata as well.

REFUSED, changing nothing, for: a document that is not an EntityDescriptor (or an aggregate holding exactly one for this entity) with the selected SPSSODescriptor; an entityID that is not this service provider's; a validUntil already passed; an encryption certificate this service cannot encrypt to; a signature that does not verify against `samlSpMetadataSigningCertificate` or a realm trust anchor when any is set (or no signature then); and a document over `saml2.spMetadataMaxBytes`. A signing certificate no XML signature method uses is skipped and named in `skipped`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/saml2` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| (the answer) | any JSON |  |  |

**200**: What was consumed: `signature`, the endpoint locations, how many signing certificates were registered, and `skipped`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string |  |  |
| `assertionConsumerServices` | list |  |  |
| `assertionConsumerServices[]` | string |  |  |
| `authnRequestsSigned` | boolean |  |  |
| `cacheDuration` | string, or null |  |  |
| `certificateUse` | string |  |  |
| `created` | boolean |  |  |
